title: TWBC -  Concession of A Festive Experience at the  Ice Rink, Calverley Grounds
description:
Tunbridge Wells Borough Council (TWBC) is inviting tenders for the concession of a Festive \r
Experience event, historically a Father Christmas event, at its annual ice rink in Calverley \r
Grounds.\r
\r
Tunbridge Wells Borough Council is inviting tenders for the concession of a Festive Experience\r
event at its annual ice rink in Calverley Grounds. The contract term will be an initial 1 year with \r
a possible three annual extensions (1+1+1), extension subject to performance review and \r
event approval. This year's event will run from 29 November 2024 - 5 January 2024. If future \r
events go ahead the ice rink will open and close at a similar time period.\r
\r
The Ice Rink has been running in Calverley Grounds for 13 years. Last season (2023-24) it \r
attracted 43,004 skaters, with increased footfall to the area from visitors watching the skaters \r
or who just come along for a walk within the grounds. Anecdotally we had in excess of 80,000 \r
visitors in the period.\r
\r
Key Dates & Timeline for Procurement\r
Tender release: Monday 15th July 2024\r
Expression of Interest Deadline: 12:00pm Monday 5th August 2024\r
Deadline for submission of completed tenders: 12:00pm Monday 12th August 2024\r
Evaluation: w/c Monday 12th August 2024\r
Appointment of contractor: w/c Monday 26th August 2024

title: The repair of Pre-cast Concrete Panels, Metal Railings, and Stairways to Crescent Road Multi Storey Car Park
description:
Tunbridge Wells Borough Council (TWBC) is looking to procure a suitable qualified contractor to carry out the following testing and concrete works. The precast cladding panels of the car park are spalling in various locations, particularly at the junctions of the handrail supports. The works will consist of completing repairs to the railings and their supports, testing the cladding panels and ramp enclosure panels, then effecting concrete repairs and protective coatings as necessary. In addition, works will be completed to the stairwells to prevent water penetration and to bring them up to a suitable standard. The site is at Crescent Road Multi Story Car Park, Crescent Road, Royal Tunbridge Wells, TN1 2LU.\r

noticeIdentifier: Drainage Works Framework 2023 - Mini Competition - Fir Tree Road, Tunbridge Wells Scheme
title: SC23206 - DFC2023 - Mini Competition - Fir Tree Road, Tunbridge Wells Scheme
description:
The Drainage Works Framework 2023 (SC22331) is used to support Kent County Council's current contracts (Highway Term Maintenance Contract, Road Asset Renewal Contract and others) to maintain it network.

The drainage works consist of the provision of labour, resources, plant and materials to carry out all works associated with drainage maintenance works and general reinstatement works on both highway and non-highway sites.

Works under £25k are awarded via direct award on a rotation basis.

Works over £25k are awarded via a mini-competition process.

This notice pertains to a mini-competition exercise that was carried out under the Drainage Works Framework 2023.

Details of this mini-competition are below listed below:
- Aim: to find a Contractor to deliver the Fir Tree Road Tunbridge Wells scheme.
- Dates: The scheme needs to be delivered between the 29 January 2024 to 04 March 2024.
- The scheme will deliver the following outputs, please note that this is not an exclusive list:
• Road closure, advanced warning signs, and letter drops.
• To carry out two trial hole trenches across the full width of the carriageway.
• To replace three existing gullies with new 450mm x 900mm gully pots, and to also install another four new 450mm 
x 900mm gully pots.
• To install two new Type 2a chambers in the carriageway.
• To install a new 2.4m dia, 4m deep Type 1 Soakaway (conventional) on the verge of the Commons to KCC 
standard. Before excavating for the soakaway, the existing turf is to be cut out, rolled up and set aside for re-use. 
Some of the best of the soil is also to be set aside for reinstating. 
• To install a total of 49m. new 225mm Twinwall pipe at various locations within the carriageway.
• To install a total of 41.45m of new 150mm Twinwall pipe from the gullies to the new chambers and from the gullies 
to the new 225mm and 150mm pipes as indicated on the plans. 
• The existing drainage pipe from existing gully to gully crossing the junction of Fir Tree Rd is the be sealed up at 
end when the gully is replaced. 
• To reinstate the trenches of the Type 4 carriageway to KCC standard detail

title: Outsourced Physiotherapy Services
description:
Background:\r
Kent Community Health NHS Foundation Trust (KCHFT) hold a prime provider contract for the delivery of musculoskeletal (MSK) physiotherapy in West Kent. In order to achieve the Key performance indicators (KPIs) associated with this contract and aligning with the expectation of collaboration with other providers it is our intention to issue an invitation to tender for providers of MSK physiotherapy in the Tunbridge Wells area.\r
\r
Access To Services:\r
KCHFT receives Physiotherapy referrals from GPs in the Tunbridge Wells and Tonbridge localities and wishes to offer those patients who are registered with these GPs an opportunity to be treated at a convenient outpatient clinic within the area. KCHFT will refer such patients to the Provider, who will only accept such referrals under this Contract. This Contract does not include patients that have self-referred or come direct from other referring parties, including direct from a GP Practice. The Provider will offer all patients who are referred via KCHFT an initial appointment for assessment.The Provider will offer the first assessment appointment for a 30 minutes slot with a physical therapist experienced in musculoskeletal disorders that will allow a thorough assessment and a treatment plan to be devised. For those patients who are deemed suitable for treatment following the initial assessment appointment, the treatment plan will continue in follow-up appointments which will last for 30 minutes each. A course of therapy will typically take between two and six sessions depending on the type and severity of the condition. The provider must offer the proposed physiotherapy service at a location within 5 miles of Royal Tunbridge Wells, to ensure a reasonable and practicable offering to referrals in relation to travel and accessibility. The Provider will ensure that all treatment facilities comply with Department of Health standards in terms of cleanliness and offer patients a safe, pleasant and suitable environment that has equitable access to services.\r
\r
Contract Term: 24 months plus three extension opportunities in tranches of 12 months (2+1+1+1 years), total potential term of 5 years.\r
\r
Forecasted Activity: (current estimated activity for this ad hoc provision, and there is no guaranteed activity or obligation from the authority)\r
New Referrals Per Week: 20\r
Average Sessions per Referral: 4\r
Forecasted Sessions per week: 80 \r
Forecasted New Referrals Per Month: 80\r
Forecasted sessions per Month: 320\r
Forecasted New Referrals Per Annum: 1040\r
Forecasted Sessions Per Annum: 4160 \r
\r
If you would like to express your interest in this opportunity, please log in / register on the Proactis e-Tendering Portal here: https://procontract.due-north.com/Login/ and register your interest against DN692299.\r
Expression of interest window closes on the 16/10/2023 @ 00:00hrs, ITT documentation will be published on 16/10/2023.\r
\r
A detailed specification of requirements will be issued at the ITT Stage.

title: Contracts for the Provision of Mortuary Services
description:
The Coroners and Justice Act 2009 places a duty on Coroners to investigate deaths 
that are referred to them if they have reason to think that: 
 The death was violent or unnatural; 
 The cause of death is unknown; or 
 The deceased died while in prison, police custody or another form of state detention. 

In some cases, the Coroner will order a Post-Mortem (PM) to establish the cause of  death, and in such cases, the deceased is taken to one of five NHS mortuaries across Kent and Medway. On behalf of the Kent Senior Coroners, KCC ensures access to body storage and PM facilities across the Kent coroner areas. 

 Contracts with Dartford and Gravesham, East Kent, Medway Maritime and Maidstone and Tunbridge Wells NHS Trusts for the provision of PM facilities are in place to fulful this requirement.

description:
Kent County Council (the Council) require a contract for a number of providers to undertake routine vegetation clearance on identified Public Rights of Way (PRoW); a statutory requirement. The contract will be split into 10 lots, combining an element of programmed work together with ad-hoc requirements including off road cycle paths.\r
\r
Public Rights of Way consist of four different levels of access:\r
\r
â€¢ Public Footpath (FP) for pedestrian use;\r
â€¢ Public Bridleway (BR) for equestrian, pedestrian and pedal cyclists use;\r
â€¢ Restricted Byway (RB) a carriageway for use by non-motorised vehicles, equestrians and pedestrians; and\r
â€¢ Byways Open to All Traffic (BW) a carriageway for use by all forms of traffic.\r
\r
The Council (on behalf of the Public Rights of Way and Access Service (PRoW)) is looking to put in place new Contracts to fulfill the statutory requirements of the PRoW team for the provision of vegetation clearance services on the Kent Public Rights of Way Network.\r
\r
The previous contract commenced in April 2018 for an initial period of 5-years with two optional 12-months extensions. Both extensions have been taken with the current extension due to expire in April 2025.\r
\r
It is anticipated that the planned Contracts will begin in April/June 2025.\r
\r
The existing multiple contracts were procured to undertake routine vegetation clearance on identified Public Rights of Way; with the contract being split into 10 lots, combining an element of programmed work together with ad-hoc requirements including off road cycle paths, with a 30-day turnaround time. The breakdown of lots are as follows:\r
\r
Lot 1 - Ashford and Folkestone & Hythe \r
Lot 2 - Canterbury and Thanet \r
Lot 3 - Dover \r
Lot 4 - Swale \r
Lot 5 - Dartford & Gravesham \r
Lot 6 - Maidstone \r
Lot 7 - Sevenoaks \r
Lot 8 - Tonbridge & Malling \r
Lot 9 - Tunbridge Wells \r
Lot 10 - North Downs Way

title: CN250226 - Ordinary Watercourse Gauging
description:
The Flood and Water Management Team at Kent County Council undertakes the council's duties as the Lead Local Flood Authority for Kent, including investigations into significant flood events.

Repeated incidences of flooding have occurred around four culverted ordinary watercourses in Kent. Two in Tunbridge Wells, the River Grom and the Southborough Stream; one in Ightham, the Busty Stream; and two in Snodland, Roman Road small watercourse and Pollard Lake Outflow.

The Supplier will be working with Kent County Council to undertake river monitoring through the implementation of gauges on the above watercourses to gather data such as but not limited to the river level, flow and velocity providing detailed monitoring, reporting, maintenance and management of the gauges installed over the contract duration.

The initial contract term is 5 years with an option to extend on an annual rolling basis for a maximum of 5 years.

title: SC23191 Coroner Removals and Transfer Service
description:
Coroners are independent judicial officers, appointed by the local authority within the coroner area. Local authorities have a legal obligation to support the work of Coroner's, to fund all the costs of the service and to provide the necessary resources to enable them to carry out their statutory obligations under the Coroners and Justice Act 2009. This includes the provision of appropriate contractual arrangements for the removal of the deceased. For the four Kent coroner areas of Mid Kent & Medway, North-West Kent, North-East Kent and Central & South-East Kent, KCC is the lead authority for the administrative areas of Kent and Medway.

There are two requirements for this service: 
Lot 1 - Coroner Removals Service and Lot 2 - Coroner Transfers Service. 

The Coroners Removals Service (Lot 1) has been separated into 15 contract areas:
1 (A) - Sevenoaks A (above A25)
1 (B) - Sevenoaks B (below A25)
1 (C) - Dartford & Gravesham 
1 (D) - Tunbridge Wells 
1 (E) - Tonbridge and Malling 
1 (F) - Medway  
1 (G) - Maidstone 
1 (H) - West Swale 
1 (I) - East Swale 
1 (J) - Ashford  
1 (K) - Canterbury  
1 (L) - Shepway
1 (M) - Thanet 
1 (N) - Dover NEK 
1 (O) - Dover CSEK

The Coroners Removals Service includes the provision of appropriate contractual arrangements for the removal of the deceased to a designated mortuary. The movement of the deceased to the mortuary constitutes a "Coroners Removal".

Where an organisation is awarded a contract area, they are responsible for providing this service throughout the specified area. They must deliver this service 24/7, 365 days a year, and in accordance with the service requirements as detailed within the specification.

The Coroners Transfers Service (Lot 2) has been separated into 2 contract areas:
2 (A) West Kent Transfers
2 (B) East Kent Transfers

In certain circumstances, it is necessary to transfer the deceased from a designated mortuary to another designated mortuary. These transfers can occur locally as a transfer between mortuaries within Kent and Medway but can occur outside of Kent. 

Where an organisation is awarded a contract area, they are responsible for providing this service throughout the specified area. They must deliver this service 24/7, 365 days a year, and in accordance with the service requirements as detailed within the specification.

Contract Length (Initial Term): 3 years.
Extension Period: up to a maximum period of 2 years (1+1).

title: Sanctuary SAFER Scheme
description:
Kent County Council are looking to commission a suitably qualified Provider to deliver the Property Security element of the Sanctuary Access for Eligible Residents SAFER Scheme. The SAFER Scheme is a new preventative service which will enable victims and survivors of domestic abuse to remain in their own home, where it is safe to do so and where the perpetrator does not live.\r
\r
The SAFER Scheme aims to improve safety, improve health, wellbeing, and prevent harm.\r
\r
The vision for the service is to provide and install approved property security measures to survivors of domestic abuse, adults and children, once the property has been adapted the household will be defined as residing in safe accommodation and will be in line with the new statutory duties introduced by the Domestic Abuse Act 2021. \r
\r
KCC are looking to commission  a property security Provider to undertake countywide property assessments, provide and install approved property security measures across the county, to improve safety and to aid in delaying a perpetrator gaining access to the property of the victim or survivor. This will lead to further positive outcomes such as, improved access to support for underserved groups, a reduction in victim risk level, repeat offences, homelessness, and the need for emergency accommodation.\r
\r
The Provider will need to demonstrate that they are cognisant of survivors needs, and able to conduct property assessments, provide and install the relevant property security measures. \r
\r
The service will be delivered countywide by a single Provider, with the option to subcontract specific works to secondary providers pre vetted by the Provider where necessary.\r
\r
The Provider will hold the contract with KCC and be ultimately responsible for the delivery of the service through the implementation and development of a responsive service that is engaged with partner agencies.\r
\r
The SAFER Scheme will be delivered through one lot, and Countywide delivery includes the following Kent local authority areas, Ashford, Canterbury, Dartford, Dover, Gravesham, Folkestone and Hythe, Maidstone, Sevenoaks, Swale, Thanet, Tonbridge and Malling, Tunbridge Wells. \r
\r
The Provider must be able to travel countywide in a timely manner.\r
\r
The contract is anticipated to commence on 1 December 2023 and will run for a period of two years, expiring 30 November 2025 with the option for two one year extensions at the discretion of the Council, unless terminated in accordance with the published Conditions of Contract.\r
\r
SQ submissions are due via the Kent Business Portal by 12pm on 31 May 2023. Please allow adequate time for uploading documents and submit responses well in advance of the closing time to avoid last minute problems.\r
\r
Interested parties are also asked to direct any questions via the Portal.
